title: Fidelity containment and cost-feedback playbook
author: Priya Desai
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook defines a structured, testable approach for containing output fidelity regressions while responding to cost and capacity signals in Redwood's serving runtime. The goal is to preserve customer-visible quality within defined tolerances while allowing the runtime to reduce unit cost and maintain latency SLOs under stress.

Intended audience
- Runtime SREs and oncall engineers
- Serving runtime product engineers
- Applied ML / model-onboarding engineers responsible for model variants
- Solutions engineers running Dedicated/Private rollouts

Scope and definitions
- Fidelity: measurable customer-facing quality of generated text or embeddings (proxy signals include embedding cosine similarity drift, eval-set pass rate, hallucination detectors, and automated eval metrics like ROUGE/BLEU/EM/accuracy on canned checks).
- Cost signal: per-request (or per-token) cost estimate derived from kernel accounting and model variant price multipliers.
- Containment action: an automated or manual change that reduces runtime resource use or switches model variant to a cheaper/less-fidelitous option (examples: quantized variant, shorter max tokens, trimmed sampling temperature, fall back to smaller model).
- Allowed fidelity window: policy-defined bounds (absolute or relative) that define tolerable degradation for a given customer tier/route.

Key principles
1. Prioritize customer-facing quality over short-term cost savings. Containment actions must be reversible and accompanied by quality monitoring.
2. Make containment decisions observable and auditable: every automated action must produce a traceable event and justification.
3. Apply progressive containment: prefer parameter tuning and cache/batching before model-variant switch.
4. Keep inexpensive, fast rollback paths and an explicit manual escalation path for high-impact customers.

Observable signals and thresholds
- Primary signals: p50/p95 latency, p99 latency, tokens/second served, per-token-cost estimate, model variant error-rate on canary prompt set, embedding drift (cosine similarity delta), auto-eval pass rate.
- Secondary signals: kernel queue length, GPU occupancy, KV cache hit ratio, request retries, gRPC error rates.

Minimum policy thresholds (example defaults)
| Signal | Warning threshold | Containment threshold | Notes |
|--------|-------------------:|----------------------:|-------|
| p95 latency (route) | 350 ms | 600 ms | measured at route-level aggregation over 1m windows |
| p99 latency | 900 ms | 2s | escalation if sustained >5 minutes |
| Per-token cost (moving 5m avg) | +15% vs baseline | +40% vs baseline | baseline is 30d rolling median |
| Embedding drift (cos sim drop) | 0.03 | 0.07 | evaluated on route-specific reference corpus |
| Canary eval pass-rate drop | 5 ppt | 15 ppt | ppt = percentage points |

Containment matrix (progressive actions)
1. Soft tuning (no model change): reduce max_response_tokens by 10–30%, reduce sampling temperature or top-p, tighten repetition_penalty, enable prefix/KV cache prefetch for hot routes.
2. Batch and cache aggression: increase batching window by 10–25% for non-interactive routes, enable shared prefix caching when identity-safe.
3. Model micro-variants: switch to quantized or 8-bit floating variant of the same model.
4. Model downgrade: route to smaller model family with documented fidelity/cost tradeoff.
5. Route-based rate limiting: apply slow-path throttle to non-critical traffic classes.
6. Emergency low-fidelity fallback: deterministic n-gram based summarization or templated replies for extreme outages.

Automation policy template (YAML-like example)
```
# policy_name: fidelity-cost-feedback-2026
triggers:
  - metric: per_token_cost_5m
    comparator: ">="
    threshold: 1.40  # 1.0 = baseline
    window: 300
    severity: high
  - metric: p95_latency_route
    comparator: ">="
    threshold: 0.6  # seconds
    window: 60
    severity: medium
actions_sequence:
  - id: "soft_tune_1"
    action: "reduce_max_tokens"
    params: { percent: 20 }
    rollback_on: ["canary_eval_drop_ppt >= 10"]
  - id: "enable_batching_aggressive"
    action: "increase_batch_window_ms"
    params: { add_ms: 15 }
  - id: "variant_quantized"
    action: "switch_model_variant"
    params: { variant: "quant-8bit" }
  - id: "variant_downgrade"
    action: "switch_model"
    params: { model_family: "redwood-lite" }
  - id: "emergency_template_fallback"
    action: "apply_template_fallback"
    params: { template_id: "low_fidelity_fallback_v1" }
```

Operational runbook (play-by-play)
1) Detection and initial triage (Oncall)\- Review alert payload: identify affected routes, model variants, and customer tiers.\- Confirm signal: check p95/p99 windows, per-token cost spike, and kernel-level metrics (GPU queue length, occupancy).\- Run quick baseline: compare to rolling 30d baseline and to same-window previous day.

2) Canary evaluation (automated/manual)\- Run the canonical canary prompt set for each impacted route against current runtime and candidate containment variants. Canary outputs to be scored by automated eval harness.\- Pass criteria: no more than X ppt drop in canary pass-rate for Standard tier; less strict thresholds for internal/beta routes.

3) Apply progressive containment\- Execute actions in the containment matrix one step at a time. After each step, wait a stabilization window (default 60–180s for soft tuning; 5–10 minutes for model variant switches) and re-evaluate canary metrics and the primary signals.\- Required observability: annotate the deployment/trace with the containment_action id and reason.

4) Monitor and iterate\- If metrics recover within thresholds, retain the change for a policy-defined cooldown (default 30 minutes) while running a more comprehensive quality sweep (10–30m).\- If metrics do not improve or quality regression exceeds rollback_on conditions, immediately roll back the last action and escalate to oncall escalation path.

5) Escalation path
- Pager duty: runtime-sre@redwood.com (primary)
- If repeat-size event or large customer impact: paging product-eng lead and solutions engineering for affected customers.
- For legal/security impact (data exposure): notify security@redwood.com immediately.

Manual rollback checklist
- Identify exact action to rollback (action id and timestamp).
- Ensure no upstream automation will re-apply the action during rollback window. Use the feature-flag lock: \"runtime.containment.lock\" = true.
- Execute rollback and validate canary and live traffic metrics for 15 minutes.
- Note the rollback in incident timeline with justification.

Testing and preflight requirements
- Every containment action must have an associated unit test in the runtime-autotest suite and a canary-run scenario in the benchmark harness.
- Poison tests: synthetic low-fidelity queries must be included to ensure fallback templates don’t leak sensitive info.
- Load test runbook: schedule a weekly simulated event where containment policies are exercised end-to-end in staging using traffic replays.

Observability and dashboards (minimum set)
- Route health dashboard: per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, per-token-cost trend, request volume, KV cache hit rate.
- Canary quality dashboard: rolling pass-rate for canary prompts per route and per-customer-tier.
- Containment actions log: chronological view of automated/manual actions, actors, and outcomes (success/failure, rollback).
- Kernel telemetry correlation: cross-filter by trace id to observe kernel-level queue depth, GPU occupancy, and active kernel variant.

Audit and compliance
- All containment decisions (automated or manual) must emit an audit event with: action_id, actor (automation or user), triggered_by (metric id and value), route, affected_customers, pre_action_metrics, post_action_metrics, canary_results. Events are retained 365 days by default.

Ownership and contacts
- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime (runtime-sre rotation), contact runtime-oncall@example.redwood.com
- Model variant owner: applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding team
- Product escalation: product-engineering lead for affected product line (contact list in team wiki)

Post-incident analysis (required for any containment that persisted > 1 hour or affected > 5 customers)\- Produce a short incident summary with root cause hypothesis, timeline of containment actions, observed impact on quality/cost, and recommended permanent mitigations (e.g., model retraining, kernel tuning, new model variant).\- Required metrics: cost delta, customer-visible fidelity delta, number of rollbacks, time-to-stabilize.

Playbook example: small incident walkthrough
Scenario: sudden token cost spike on "chat-completion" route causing p95 latency to rise to 750ms and per-token cost +60%
1. Alert fired (policy: per_token_cost_5m >= 1.4)
2. Oncall runs canary set: small drop in canary pass-rate (6 ppt)
3. Apply soft_tune_1 (reduce_max_tokens 20%)
4. Re-evaluate 90s later: p95 reduced to 420ms, per-token cost reduced to +18%, canary drop stable at 7 ppt (within Standard threshold)
5. Place containment on 30m cooldown and notify product for customer comms if effected customers > 2
6. Post-incident: schedule a variant benchmark comparing quant-8bit and redwood-lite on the exact request surface.

Appendix A: sample CLI commands
- Query affected routes:
  rcli routes list --filter "metric:per_token_cost>1.2" --since 10m
- Run canary prompt set (local harness):
  python infra/tools/canary_runner.py --route chat-completion --variant current --output /tmp/canary.json
- Apply containment action (manual override):
  rcli runtime contain apply --route chat-completion --action reduce_max_tokens --percent 20 --note "manual containment by oncall"
- Lock automation to prevent reapplication:
  rcli feature-flag set runtime.containment.lock true --expiry 30m --note "incident rollback in progress"

Appendix B: policy parameter guidance
- Window sizing: prefer shorter windows (60–300s) for latency-driven triggers, longer windows (5–15m) for cost signals to avoid transient noise.
- Canary set construction: include 15–50 prompts per route with a mix of short/long sequences, edge-case tokens, and privacy-sensitive examples that must never be returned in fallback templates.
- Tiered thresholds: enterprise customers have half the allowed fidelity-degradation window compared to standard/free tiers.

Appendix C: related artifacts and links
- Execution stitching and fallback orchestration (design doc) — see related_pages for link id
- Canary harness repository: git@github.com:redwood/canary-harness
- Runtime containment audit sink: kafka://infra.events.runtime.containment
